desc: Re-evaluate the unimodal assumption: For a fixed i, is f(j) = distinct(middle) + distinct(suffix) guaranteed to be unimodal? The middle distinct count is non-decreasing as j increases, and the suffix distinct count is non-increasing as j increases. The sum of a non-decreasing and a non-increasing function is indeed unimodal (first non-decreasing, then non-increasing), so early termination when the value stops increasing is valid.

Inspect the current code for off-by-one errors: Ensure `left` is computed for i up to N-1, `right` for j+1 up to N, and the loops cover all valid i (1..N-2) and j (i+1..N-1). Also ensure `right[N+1]` is defined and used correctly.
Refactor the code to use a frequency array (since A_i ≤ N) instead of a dict for O(1) updates, and ensure all boundary conditions are handled correctly.
Test the solution on the provided sample inputs, edge cases (N=3, all identical, all distinct), and random small cases against a brute-force O(N^2) solution to validate correctness.
Produce the final, polished Python solution with proper input parsing, O(N) time and O(N) space, and ensure it reads from stdin and writes to stdout.
